data.title: blog/: BRANDING.md — Web 2.0 bloggy design direction (glossy gradients, sidebar, badges) for /blog writing site

data.to:
Write blog/BRANDING.md — the design brief for a new sub-site at /blog that hosts Forrest's writing.

WHY: Every top-level folder in this repo is a design direction whose BRANDING.md is the source of truth and whose index.html is the rendering of it (see .claude/skills/brand-page). The brief comes first; the page is generated from it.

USER'S ASK, VERBATIM: "i want to make a new site /blog for my writing. the branding should be bloggy and web 2.0".

DIRECTION: Web 2.0 blog, played straight and seriously the way vhs/ plays the TV-VCR straight — glossy gradient headers with reflections, rounded corners, 1-2px borders with inner highlights, Lucida Grande / Georgia body, striped or tiled body background, a real right sidebar (about blurb, blogroll, tag cloud, archives by month, orange RSS badge), permalinks, post meta lines, footer badges. Circa 2005-2008 Blogger/WordPress/Movable Type, not a retro pastiche that winks at itself.

DECISIONS ALREADY MADE (do not re-litigate):
- This is a destination at /blog/, NOT a viewport bucket in sites.config.json. Buckets 500-1400 are all taken, the built root page does not scroll, and a blog must scroll. It stays standalone.
- Even so, the brief must not specify anything that would violate the sub-site authoring contract in CLAUDE.md (site-prefixed ids, relative asset urls, separate style.css, own scroll container), so mapping it later stays possible.
- Depth and format should match sibling briefs (vhs/BRANDING.md, memphis/BRANDING.md): the direction, a named palette table, type, layout, motion, voice.

SCOPE: brief only. FA-32 builds the page.

data.body: Plan written. Brief spec: 9 sections mirroring vhs/memphis (direction+3 rules+voice, palette w/ named tokens + measured contrast, type, gloss/bevel recipes, layout+sidebar modules, content model, motion, what-this-is-not, page application+test). Governing discipline: 'the chrome is glossy, the writing is not' + 'every widget is load-bearing' + 'it is 2006 sincerely, not 1998 ironically'. Hexes proposed as starting values; implementer must compute WCAG ratios and darken stops (the sheen composite over the blue is the pair that forces it). Decisions: no webfont (system stacks only), Feed Orange never carries a letterform (white feed glyph + blue word beside it), no comment UI, no url() in style.css so the shared stylesheet survives post pages one dir deeper.

Brief written and committed (85f4879), 700 lines / 40KB, blog/BRANDING.md only. Decisions beyond the plan, all recorded in the brief: (1) Computed WCAG on the proposed hexes and darkened three of them until the sheen-composited ground passes — Kubrick Blue #1F5C96 -> #1B528A (4.59 -> 5.11 composited), Feed Orange Deep #C64600 -> #A03900 (3.71 -> 4.69), Beta Green #3F7A0C -> #316209 (3.69 -> 4.74), Kubrick Deep #123F6B -> #103A63, Meta Grey #6E7378 -> #686D72 (4.54 -> 4.95 on Alt Row). (2) Added one token the plan did not list, --blue-pale / Kubrick Pale #CFE0F0, because a pale-blue tagline cannot clear 4.5 on Kubrick Blue under the reflection (4.37 at best) — so the masthead splits at the 50% hard stop: white wordmark above it, Kubrick Pale tagline below on Kubrick Deep at 8.6. That split is now a layout rule. (3) Reworked .blog-gloss around a --gloss-fill custom property with the bottom half derived from a black overlay instead of a per-family deep token, so 'fill + sheen is the worst case' is a single checkable contrast rule across blue/orange/green. (4) The white feed glyph on Feed Orange measures 2.9, below even the 3:1 non-text floor, so the brief declares the chiclet decorative and never the only affordance — the word Subscribe inside the same <a> carries the meaning. (5) Focus rings are Hyperlink Blue on paper, not Sky Highlight (2.7 on white). (6) Titles are sans (--font-title) — the plan left it open. Trimmed hard from a 847-line first draft to hit the plan's 450-700 range.

Review of 85f4879 (blog/BRANDING.md, 700 lines) — cold read against the plan, the sibling briefs, and build.js. VERDICT: PASS, with two classes of defect fixed inline (ecf8110).

WHAT I REVIEWED. Full brief; plan acceptance criteria 1-14 one by one; vhs/BRANDING.md and memphis/BRANDING.md for house format, depth and voice; root CLAUDE.md's authoring contract plus build.js itself (scopeSelector, transformStatements, the wrapper div at line 290 and the boot at line 301); an independent WCAG 2.x recomputation of every published ratio.

CONTRAST — ALL FIFTEEN CORRECT. Recomputed relative luminance from the hexes and compared to the brief's table. Every value matches to the published precision: 12.63/15.91/5.23/4.95/6.44/7.38 on paper; 11.62 white on Kubrick Deep; 8.62 Kubrick Pale on Kubrick Deep; 11.54 Body Grey on Yellow Fade; and the three failures recorded as failures (2.94 Feed Orange, 2.71 Sky Highlight, 2.05 Sticker Green). The sheen compositing is right and the arithmetic is the arithmetic the brief describes: c' = c + 0.18(1-c) per channel in sRGB gives exactly #44719F, #B15D2E and #567E35, measuring 5.11, 4.69 and 4.74 — the three published composites. The composite is also genuinely the worst case, because §4.1's ::after ramps the sheen from 0.18 at the top edge down to 0 at the 50% break, so no pixel under a label is lighter than the measured one. Kubrick Blue at #1B528A is 8.01 uncomposited and 5.11 composited, which confirms the brief's own claim that the sheen is what forced the blue darker.

FIXED INLINE (1) — wrong wrapper-selector form, five normative CSS blocks. The brief wrote its rules as '#site-blog .blog-entry-body', '#site-blog .blog-wrap', '#site-blog .blog-entry:target' and, worst, '#site-blog { background... }' for the page ground. build.js scopeSelector() prefixes every authored selector with '#site-blog', so those compile to '#site-blog #site-blog .x' and match nothing; standalone they match nothing either, since the wrapper div is created by build.js (line 290) and not authored — zero of the six sibling stylesheets contain a '#site-' selector and zero sibling index.html files contain an id="site-*" element. Left as written, FA-32 either ships a blog with no ground at all or invents a wrapper div and puts a duplicate id in the combined document, which is the exact failure §9 spends a bullet warning about. Rules are now bare class selectors, the ground moved to 'body' (which the build rewrites to the wrapper correctly), the §9 pseudo-class example lost its prefix, and §9's wrapper bullet now states the rule and the reason. Mechanical fix, no design decision touched.

FIXED INLINE (2) — two ratios citing the wrong ground. Both still pass, so this is precision, not a contrast failure. §5's masthead says the tagline sits on the darkened half '(measured 8.6)', but 8.6 is Kubrick Pale on flat Kubrick Deep, which is the nav strip; the masthead's darkened half is Kubrick Blue under an 0.18-0.30 black overlay, lightest pixel #164371, where Kubrick Pale measures 7.5. §5's tag pill says its hover tint measures 5.6, but pills sit on Alt Row, so the tint composites to #E0ECF7 and Hyperlink Blue on it is 5.4; 5.6 is the over-white value. Both corrected with the real ground named.

INTERNAL CONSISTENCY — clean otherwise. All 23 palette tokens appear in both the table and the :root block, in both directions. Every var(--x) reference in the whole file resolves to a token defined somewhere in it — checked programmatically, zero orphans. Layout arithmetic closes: 940 wrapper - 24 padding = 916 = 620 main + 28 gutter + 268 sidebar. Radius ceiling, sheen cap and the 1px border rule are stated consistently everywhere they recur.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. 1-13 met. §2 carries 23 tokens against a floor of 16, with the sheen-composited masthead worst case published as required and the three non-text colors explicitly recorded. §4 has five named recipes with real CSS. §7 has exactly five effects, the Yellow Fade keyframe and the reduced-motion block. §8 has seven rows including all five required near misses. §9 covers every contract item on the list. Criterion 14 is met on voice — declarative, deadpan, no second person, no hedging, and the brief never winks; it now sits at 703 lines against a 450-700 target, a 3-line overage introduced by this review's own corrections, not by the implementer.

NON-BLOCKING NITS, left alone deliberately. §7 describes the focus ring as 'square, hairline' while specifying 'outline: 2px' — wording only, and §4.6's 1px rule is about borders, not outlines. §4.3 writes 'box-shadow: 0 1px 2px var(--shade)' literally where --sh-1 is defined to be exactly that. Neither is worth a rework cycle and neither can mislead FA-32.

The brief reads as a sibling of vhs/ and memphis/, not as generated output: it makes real judgment calls, names its own failure modes, and its three 'things to hold onto' are load-bearing rather than decorative. It is buildable as it now stands.
